newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends low on genuine dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends low on genuine dollar demand.

text.p: COLOMBO, Dec 23 (Rupee) - The Sri Lanka rupee closed lower against the dollar on Monday as banks bought the U.S. currency to cover imports, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 56.72 to the dollar after opening at 56.65. It closed at 56.60 on Friday.
Overnight call money closed at 20 percent after rising in the morning to 29 percent, due to seasonal demand for the local currency, dealers said.
"There is a shortfall (of rupees) in the market due to heavy cash withdrawals to meet festival expenses," a Standard Chartered Bank dealer said.
"People are carrying a lot of money in their pockets. So there is a shortage in the money market," he said.
The tightness would ease early next year, after the money starts returning to the system, he added.
The Sri Lankan foreign exchange market will be closed on Tuesday and Wednesday for Christmas.
